no_question.record:
S/PV.9461, p. 2. On 30 October 2023, the Council voted on United Kingdom draft S/2023/808. All 15 members voted in favour and the Council President announced unanimous adoption as resolution 2704 (2023).

On 30 October 2023, the Security Council unanimously adopted Resolution 2704 (2023) via UK draft S/2023/808 [S/PV.9461, p. 2]. The resolution extends the UN Verification Mission in Colombia until 31 October 2024 [OPERATIVE]. It expresses the Council's willingness to collaborate with the Colombian Government on further mandate extensions based on inter-party agreement [OPERATIVE].

Regarding the Government–EMC ceasefire, the Council expressed willingness to consider monitoring and verification protocols contingent upon the Secretary-General confirming a ceasefire and updating on Resolution 2694 implementation [ADDITIONAL]. Brazil emphasized Colombia's sovereign will, requesting Council authorization for EMC verification once mature [working_notes]. Ghana, speaking for African members, welcomed the extension and supported EMC monitoring under Secretary-General conditions, pledging to encourage progress on the Ethnic Chapter for Afro-Colombian and Indigenous peoples [working_notes].

The Council preserved a shared position on extending the Mission's core mandate while maintaining flexibility for future ceasefire verification mechanisms dependent on verified ground realities. All 15 members voted in favour, affirming the collective commitment to the peace process in Colombia [working_notes].

no_question.record:
S/PV.9331, p. 2. On 30 May 2023, the Council voted 15 in favour on United States draft S/2023/378 and adopted it unanimously as resolution 2682 (2023). The President announced adoption and the meeting ended. No national explanation of vote appears in this meeting record.

On 30 May 2023, the Security Council unanimously adopted Resolution 2682 (2023) [S/PV.9331, p. 2], extending UNAMI's mandate to 31 May 2024. The resolution prioritizes inclusive political dialogue and reconciliation with full women's participation. It formally authorizes the mission's continued operational framework under Council authority, supported by Iraq's request [Working Note 1].

The Council also mandated an independent strategic review of UNAMI by 31 March 2024 [Working Note 2]. This review must consult Iraq, UN agencies, Member States, regional organizations, independent experts, civil society, and Kuwait. Iraq's government expressed support via a letter dated 18 May 2023 [Working Note 2]. The review will assess threats, mandate relevance, and recommend structural changes to support regional cooperation. The Secretary-General is required to report biannually on UNAMI's fulfilment of responsibilities [Working Note 1]. No national explanations of vote were recorded in this meeting.
